q: Which Boolean operator narrows a search so that results must contain both search terms?
x: AND returns only pages that contain every joined term, so it gives fewer, more focused results. OR widens a search by accepting pages with either term.

q: Which query returns pages that mention at least one of the two words solar and wind?
x: OR accepts a page that contains either word or both. AND needs both words, NOT drops pages that mention wind, and the quotation marks ask for the exact phrase "solar wind".

q: Putting a search in quotation marks, as in `"climate change in Pakistan"`, tells the search engine to:
o: find pages in any order of words
x: Quotation marks ask for the words together in exactly that order. Leaving words out is done with NOT or a minus sign, not with quotation marks.

q: Four web pages contain these words: W1 "Lahore weather", W2 "Karachi traffic", W3 "Islamabad weather", W4 "Karachi weather report". Which pages match `(Lahore OR Karachi) AND weather`?
x: A page must mention Lahore or Karachi and must also mention weather. W1 and W4 pass both tests; W2 lacks weather and W3 mentions neither city.

q: A student wants results about scholarships only from the website hec.gov.pk. Which search does this?
x: The `site:` operator limits results to one website or domain. `filetype:` limits the kind of file (such as pdf), and the minus sign would exclude pages mentioning that site.

q: Which search finds only PDF documents about the water cycle?
x: `filetype:pdf` restricts results to PDF files. `site:` expects a website, and the minus sign removes pages that mention pdf.

q: When evaluating an online source, a student checks whether the writer is a qualified expert working for a known organisation. Which criterion is being checked?
x: Authority is about who wrote the source and whether they are qualified to write it. Currency is about how recent the information is.

q: A student sends an online questionnaire to her classmates and collects their answers herself. The data she collects is:
x: Data collected first-hand by the researcher for her own study is primary data. Secondary data was collected by someone else, for example figures from a published report.

q: Four web pages contain these words: P1 "python" and "snake"; P2 "python" only; P3 "snake" only; P4 "python" and "code". Which pages match `python NOT snake`?
x: The page must contain python and must not contain snake. P2 and P4 qualify; P1 mentions snake and P3 lacks python. Answering P2 only wrongly drops P4, which never mentions snake.

q: An email that looks like it is from your bank asks you to confirm your password by clicking a link. What is the safest response?
o: Click the link, but enter the password only if the page shows the bank logo
Do not click; contact the bank through its official number or website
Reply to the email asking the sender to confirm that it is really the bank
Click the link from a computer that has an up-to-date antivirus program
x: This is a typical phishing message: a bank never asks for a password by email. Checking through the bank’s own official contact avoids the fake link; a copied logo, a reply that reaches the attacker, or antivirus software does not make the link safe.

q: An entrepreneur is best described as a person who:
o: starts a new business and takes on its financial risk
works for a fixed salary in a large company
only lends money to other businesses
only buys shares on the stock market
x: An entrepreneur turns an idea into a new business and accepts the risk of loss in hope of profit. A salaried employee does not carry the business's risk.

q: In the five-stage design thinking process (Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype, Test), which stage comes first?
x: Design thinking starts by understanding the users and their needs (Empathize). Only then is the problem defined and are ideas generated.

q: In design thinking (Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype, Test), which stage comes straight after Ideate?
x: After many ideas are generated (Ideate), the best ones are turned into simple models (Prototype), which are then tried out with users (Test). Define comes before Ideate.

q: A team quickly draws paper mock-ups of an app's screens so that users can try them. Which design thinking stage is this?
x: Building a simple, cheap model of a solution is the Prototype stage. Ideate is generating ideas, before any model is built.

q: Which activity belongs to the Empathize stage of design thinking?
o: Interviewing and observing users to understand their problems
Letting users try a mock-up and recording feedback
x: Empathize is about understanding users by talking to and watching them. Writing a problem statement is Define, brainstorming is Ideate and trying a mock-up is Test.

q: Which of these belongs in the market analysis section of a business plan?
o: Projected profit for the next three years
Who the target customers and main competitors are
The loan amount the business is requesting
x: Market analysis studies the customers, their needs, the market size and the competition. Projected profit and the loan request belong to the financial section, and the founders' roles to the management section.

q: A small online tutoring business has fixed costs of Rs 60,000 a month. Each lesson sold earns Rs 300 more than its own cost. How many lessons a month must it sell to break even?
x: Break-even is where the earnings per lesson cover the fixed costs: 60,000 ÷ 300 = 200 lessons. Below 200 lessons the business makes a loss.

q: In a business plan, the target market is:
o: the place where the business keeps its stock
the total money the business expects to earn
the specific group of customers the business aims to sell to
x: A target market is a clearly defined group of likely customers, for example students in a city. Aiming at everyone online is too broad to plan for; expected earnings are a financial projection.

q: In a SWOT analysis, a large new competitor entering the market is listed as a:
x: Threats are outside factors that could harm the business, and a new competitor is outside the business. Weaknesses are internal, such as a small team or little money.

q: A financial projection assumes an app has 400 paying users in month 1, gains 100 more paying users each month, and each user pays Rs 200 a month. What is the projected revenue in month 3?
x: Month 1 has 400 users, month 2 has 500 and month 3 has 600, so month 3 revenue is 600 × 200 = Rs 120,000. Rs 300,000 is the total for all three months, not month 3 alone.
